card.name: Small words in old-style prose
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as on, to, I, he, our or their in older formal English prose, such as 19th-century essays and books. They sit just before a noun or clause, like 'explicable on the theory' or 'the best he could'.

modes.label: Preposition after adjective or verb
modes.description: A preposition follows an adjective or verb in a formal argument.
modes.example: is explicable<< on>> the theory of natural selection.

modes.label: Pronoun in 'best I/he can'
modes.description: A pronoun comes after 'the best' or 'analysis' and before 'can' or 'could'.
modes.example: make the best analysis<< I>> can of what is essential to a sign

modes.label: Pronoun or possessive after a verb
modes.description: A pronoun or possessive follows a verb and leads into its object.
modes.example: make a caucus and lay<< their>> plan for introducing certain persons

card.plain: It fires on little connecting words in old-fashioned book prose, right before the phrase continues.
